parameters.text:
=You are an AI Manager Alert Filter for Tulip Flowers.

The input may come from:
- Text messages
- Audio transcriptions
- AI-generated image descriptions

Message Type:
{{ $json.messageType }}

Content:
{{ $json.input }}

Set needs_attention = true only if the content indicates a serious business risk, including:

- customer complaint
- negative sentiment or dissatisfaction
- refund or replacement request
- wrong, damaged, missing, or poor-quality order
- delivery problem
- payment issue
- legal threat, bad review, or complaint to authorities
- VIP or urgent corporate issue
- same-day delivery problem that risks losing the customer

Otherwise return needs_attention = false.

Base your decision on the meaning of the content, not exact keywords.

OUTPUT RULES -- follow exactly. The mobile app matches these values against a
fixed list, so any value outside the lists below is shown to managers as "Other".

priority: exactly one of
  urgent   (legal threat, authority complaint, public review threat, paid order not delivered)
  high     (refund, payment issue, wrong order, delivery failure)
  medium   (dissatisfaction or complaint that may escalate)
  low      (normal conversation)

department: exactly one of
  sales | operations | delivery | finance | support | management

category: exactly one of
  customer_complaint | customer_dissatisfaction | refund_request |
  delivery_problem | payment_issue | wrong_or_damaged_order |
  quality_issue | legal_threat | vip_issue | general_inquiry

All three must be lowercase with underscores. Never invent a value outside these lists,
never use spaces, and never use Title Case.

summary, reason and action: one short sentence each, written in ARABIC.

Return only the required structured JSON.

nodes.name: Needs attention?
nodes.notes: Reads the Firestore CREATE RESPONSE, so the shape is REST -- fields.needs_attention.booleanValue, not $json.needs_attention. Routine traffic must never fire a phone.

nodes.name: Get Device Tokens
nodes.notes: Same Firestore credential as the alerts write -- the datastore scope covers this read. Returns { documents: [...] }, and omits the key entirely when no device has registered yet.

nodes.name: Build FCM Payloads
nodes.notes: Emits one item per device. Returns zero items when nobody has registered, which simply ends the branch.

nodes.name: Send to FCM
nodes.notes: Uses a Google Service Account credential scoped to https://www.googleapis.com/auth/firebase.messaging -- NOT the Firestore OAuth2 credential, which carries the datastore scope only and 403s here. neverError is deliberate: FCM v1 takes one token per request, so without it one dead token aborts the run and everyone behind it gets nothing.
